118.visualIdea: A 100-dot grid on a dark ground. Dots fill one by one in pale coral until 86 of 100 are lit, the remaining 14 staying as dim outlines. A large counting '86%' resolves beside the grid, with a small caption 'of one utility's third-party supply customers paid MORE than the standard rate' and a quiet source line 'Connecticut Office of Consumer Counsel'. The proportion becoming visible IS the point — best real footage available was a generic 'person checking documents' shot that depicts nothing about this figure.

119.visualIdea: Two numbers resolve in sequence on a dark ground: '$50,000,000' counting up, then beneath it '278,000 households' counting up, joined by a thin drawn connector rule. A small dateline chip reads 'New York — April'. Below, a single line: 'nine affiliated suppliers ordered to return'. The scale of the refund against the number of households is the entire point of the film's biggest number — best real footage was a state capitol building exterior, which depicts none of it.

124.visualIdea: Two labeled rate cards sit side by side against a dark ground, mimicking two lines lifted off a bill: left 'YOUR SUPPLY RATE' with a placeholder figure in cents per kWh, right 'UTILITY DEFAULT RATE' with a lower one. A vertical divider draws down between them, then the left card's figure ticks visibly higher than the right and a thin bracket labels the gap 'the difference you're paying'. The narration says 'put the two side by side' verbatim — a stock shot of two coworkers discussing paperwork does not show a rate comparison.
